summary: Dispatch, run-status, committed-slice integration, coordination preflight, and runtime-blocker-taxonomy tools.

tools.notes: MCP-only agent role dispatch for worker, reviewer, and redteam. The normal call supplies only role and subject. On every dispatch the launcher reads the role model from repo-root agent-launch.toml and derives app/backend through the neutral model registry; typed app/model are explicit per-dispatch overrides only. Missing, malformed, or unknown role configuration refuses actionably with no family fallback. Same-user stdio MCP is not an authentication boundary; the real boundary is the launcher sandbox plus work-record admission. Caller-supplied identity carriers (request payload, prompt text, ambient env, argv, claimed_identity.role) are refused and never become selection authority. Worker and reviewer accept a WK or slice; redteam also accepts an IN. Non-dispatchable subjects refuse with work_record_readiness_failure. Reviewer mutation authority is always empty. A canonical implementation slice already in review with a launcher-verified exact committed target is reviewed against that same subject without changing its declared delivery write_scope; other reviewer subjects with non-empty write_scope refuse with role_policy_violation / reviewer_write_scope_nonempty and require a separate findings-only review unit. Confined Claude and Codex sessions receive exactly one launcher-owned host wiki-MCP server through two private named FIFOs bound into the final bubblewrap namespace and the pinned copy-only relay; exact initialize and tools/list readiness is mandatory. Agy is unsupported and fails closed. Refusals use stable runtime-blocker taxonomy codes. Route worker/reviewer/redteam dispatch through this MCP tool only; if the launch backend is unconfigured, report the blocker rather than falling back to wrappers, shell, env, another transport, or bwrap changes.
use_when: The dispatch_role_call intent has a dispatchable workspace_validate_dispatch result for the same unit and role.
do_not_use_when: Readiness is unknown; use workspace_validate_dispatch first.
The task asks about an existing run; use workspace_agent_run_status or workspace_agent_run_wait.
requires_prior_state: Same-unit same-role workspace_validate_dispatch result with dispatchable=true.

When CCE/Node Engine refusal output includes a valid worker_admission.recovery.v1 object, treat it as the primary recovery projection: pack_result.recovery is current-decision recovery, while top-level route-problem recovery applies before a pack_result exists. Both are advisory, non-authorizing, resubmission-only guidance; they do not satisfy review evidence, accepted authority, launcher policy, or admission. Legacy reason-fact recovery is compatibility-only when no valid recovery object is present. tools.notes: Monitor-handle status query for workspace_agent_dispatch. Caller-supplied identity carriers are refused before handle lookup. Monitor handles are opaque server-issued tokens scoped to subject and role; subject mismatch, replay, and unknown handles refuse via the monitor_handle_* taxonomy. Reports the CHILD lifecycle vocabulary launching, running, succeeded, failed, or cancelled. With no launch executor configured every handle resolves to MONITOR_HANDLE_UNKNOWN (status=null) - a stable refusal, not the normal posture. Free/local output is prose-only under DEC-0128, so structured_role_result.valid:false on a terminal success is EXPECTED. NOT read-only for a managed exact-slice worker run: polling a terminal managed worker advances that run launcher-owned post-worker lifecycle, which may prepare review state, integrate the slice, update Git refs, and update canonical slice status. terminal:true means the COMPLETE managed run is finalized and is the only stable terminal result; child_terminal reports only that the child ended, so terminal can stay false after child success, with a lifecycle_resolution carrying the action to take.
use_when: The run_monitoring intent asks for status, output, failure, or completion of an already dispatched run.
do_not_use_when: The task is a new role launch; use workspace_validate_dispatch first.
No monitor handle is available; ask for it instead of searching, reading records, or relaunching.

tools.notes: Bounded-wait companion to run-status: waits for a dispatched run to finish or until a bounded polling window expires, one response per call. Omit timeout_ms for the client-safe 60000 ms default. Out-of-range or non-integer timeout_ms/poll_interval_ms are refused, never clamped. Shares identity-carrier refusals, workspace resolution, and the monitor_handle_* taxonomy. Free/local output is prose-only under DEC-0128, so structured_role_result.valid:false on a terminal success is EXPECTED. NOT read-only for a managed exact-slice worker run: like run-status, polling advances that run launcher-owned post-worker lifecycle, which may prepare review state, integrate the slice, update Git refs, and update canonical slice status. The window bounds the whole call - after the child exits the route keeps waiting, on the same deadline and poll interval, for the lifecycle to finalize - so terminal:true means the COMPLETE managed run is finalized while child_terminal reports only that the child ended. A lifecycle blocked on a caller action returns promptly with that exact next_action; timed_out:true is a clean window expiry, not a failed run - retry the same monitor_handle, never relaunch.
use_when: The run_monitoring intent asks to wait briefly for an already dispatched run to finish.
do_not_use_when: The task is a new role launch; use workspace_validate_dispatch first.
No monitor handle is available; ask for it instead of searching, reading records, or relaunching.

tools.notes: Read-only schema-backed runtime blocker taxonomy: the canonical code catalog, categories, the deterministic degraded-state mapping, and the bootstrap-state subset. Dispatch (workspace_agent_dispatch) and the launcher must select blocker codes from this taxonomy rather than inventing ad hoc strings. reviewer_write_scope_nonempty is a structured reason on role_policy_violation (not a separate code); canonical committed implementation slices in review use launcher-owned exact-target admission with empty reviewer mutation authority, while other non-empty reviewer subjects require a separate findings-only review unit.

Read-only coordinator/orchestrator preflight: reports role, caller/session role, subject, allowed durable write surfaces (docs/, wiki/), the implementation/test edit prohibition, repo/docs/wiki writability, available structured dispatch/validation routes, and active runtime blocker codes. A fully read-only mount surfaces as read_only_mount (filesystem category), not as role policy. Caller-supplied identity carriers are refused; role and caller_session_role are caller-asserted introspection knobs.

Separate orchestrator continuation for exact committed-slice integration. Reviewer and redteam output is independently retained advisory evidence with no admission or veto authority; completion never calls integration. The orchestrator may accept, reject, or defer individual comments, but those dispositions and the request itself are not authorization. CCE owns every configured organization-policy decision. Paid-tier presence alone configures no gate and implies no verdict. A configured CCE gate fails closed when its decision is missing, unavailable, malformed, unratified, denied, or target-mismatched. With no configured gate, DEC-0133 free-substrate behavior is reported honestly as non-audit. Input is closed to repo alias, canonical slice subject, and comment dispositions; refs, SHAs, receipts, policy verdicts, CCE attestations, liveness claims, and other authority carriers are rejected. The server derives the exact target/ref/state and performs CAS-safe idempotent integration exactly once.
use_when: A committed implementation slice is parked after review preparation and the orchestrator is ready to disposition advisory comments and request integration.
do_not_use_when: The task is to dispatch or monitor a reviewer; use workspace_agent_dispatch or workspace_agent_run_status.
The caller intends to supply a ref, SHA, receipt, policy verdict, CCE attestation, or other authority carrier.
requires_prior_state: A canonical committed implementation slice in review with launcher-owned frozen target state.

tools.notes: Orchestrator/operator continuation for byte-identical publication of the exact terminal candidate. Reviewer and redteam results are advisory only: clean output cannot authorize and findings cannot veto. CCE alone decides a configured organization-policy gate; paid tier alone configures no policy. Configured missing, unavailable, malformed, unratified, denied, or target-mismatched evidence fails closed; no gate follows DEC-0133 free substrate and reports non-audit. The server derives C/L/W, candidate-bound record, remote, branch, and pull request. After restart it reads only the fixed current-candidate ref: a present target is mechanically recovered, while an absent ref triggers deterministic first-cycle construction and absent-ref expected-old CAS before exact validation. Monitor memory, historical bindings, and legacy candidate refs are irrelevant. Per DEC-0169, later landing-ref movement neither invalidates review nor blocks publication of unchanged C; merge readiness belongs to the configured merge actor and CCE policy. Missing, ambiguous, moved, or inconsistent required Git/object/record/remote facts other than normal current-ref absence refuse. Caller input is closed to a workspace alias and canonical WK-#### assigned_unit.
use_when: A terminal candidate is frozen and quiescent and the orchestrator is ready to request its exact forge publication.
do_not_use_when: The work record is still active, or an implementation slice or managed run is still open; finish the lifecycle first.
The task asks to merge, approve, rebase, or update an existing branch; the forge and organization policy own those.
authoritative_for: launcher-owned forge branch creation and pull-request create-or-observe
requires_prior_state: A launcher-frozen exact terminal candidate with canonical initiative assignment and a quiescent lifecycle.
Launcher-configured landing branch and a forge credential available host-side to the trusted server.
